meta_title: DropLane — Know what the day really paid
meta_description: DropLane records a courier's drives on its own, takes the fuel, the parking and the running costs off the takings, and tells you what the hour actually paid. Plus a mileage record ready for your accountant, in twenty-four languages, all on your phone.
language_title: Read this site in your language
language_note: The app itself speaks twenty-four languages — the rest are on their way here.
langbar_rest: Pick yours — the app speaks it too.
hero_h1: Know what the day really paid.
hero_lede: Start driving. That's it. DropLane records every drive and the route it actually took, takes the costs off the takings, and has your hourly rate waiting before you're through the door.
money_h2: Two days. Same kilometres. Not the same money.
money_intro: Both of these are three drives and about eighty-five kilometres, off the same phone, in the same van. A mileage app files them as more or less the same day. They are thirty-four dollars apart.
money_note: Kilometres are the easy half, and the half that tells you nothing. Which day was worth getting up for is in the other column — and that is the column DropLane fills in for you, on the day, without you writing anything down.
day_h2: What did the day actually pay?
day_intro: $316.39 sounds like a good day. Five hours and fifty-six minutes and $17.75 of costs later, it worked out at $43.22 an hour. That is the number nobody driving has, and the one DropLane hands you before you're through the door.
day_film1_body: Two drives, 50.8 km, $298.64 kept — and one still to sort. Nothing was typed in.
day_film2_body: Tick what goes in, pick portrait or landscape, and the PDF for the accountant is ready to send.
day_film3_title: And what the hour really paid
day_film3_body: $43.22 an hour after costs, $11.76 a kilometre, and the ATO claim worked out behind it.
day_tally_lead: One day — 50.8 km, two drives, 5 h 56 min
day_note: One day's figures, straight off the app in the films above. Yours will be different — the point is having them on the day, in the van, instead of finding out in April.
how_h2: Three steps, and two of them aren't yours
how_intro: There is no start button in DropLane, on purpose. Nobody remembers to press one at six in the morning with a van full of parcels.

how_steps.title: Turn it on once
how_steps.body: Install the app and allow location in the background. That's the last bit of setup there is.

how_steps.title: Drive
how_steps.body: Every drive saves itself, with the route, the stops, and how long you were at each one.

how_steps.title: Sort it in a tap
how_steps.body: Business, empty, on the way to a pick-up, or personal. The totals and the tax figure follow on their own.

how_proof: Then the days stack up on their own. Pick a week, a month or your own dates, tick what goes in, and the PDF for the accountant is one tap away — built from drives you never had to log.
features_intro: Built by a courier with ten years on the road, for the job as it really is.

features.title: What the day actually paid
features.body: Earnings in, fuel and costs out, and the number that matters at the bottom — per day, week, month.

features.title: What an hour really pays
features.body: Fuel, finance and insurance spread across the days you work, so the hourly figure is the true one.

features.title: Mileage without touching the phone
features.body: Drives record themselves in the background, from the moment you pull away to the moment you park.

features.title: Records ready for your accountant
features.body: A PDF with every drive, its route and its date. Mileage rates built in for seventeen countries.

features.title: Stops and waiting time
features.body: See how long you sat at each drop or depot, without writing anything down.

features.title: Nothing leaves your phone
features.body: No account to make, no tracking, no ads. Your route history is yours, backed up only to your own iCloud.

features.title: Renewals
features.body: Type the reading once and DropLane keeps it ticking from the kilometres it tracks — so service and roadworthy warnings can count down in kilometres, not just dates.

features.title: Your vehicle
features.body: Log services, tyres, and repairs here — with the invoice photo attached, it's your full garage history in your pocket.

features.title: Fuel card
features.body: Set the price your card charges per litre. Log litres when you fill up and DropLane works out the cost.

pricing_intro: Fourteen days free. No card to start, and nothing locked behind a higher tier.

faq_intro: Straight answers, from someone who does the job.

faq.q: Isn't this just another mileage tracker?
faq.a: It records mileage the same way, without a start button. The difference is what happens after: your takings go in, the fuel, parking and running costs come off, and the app tells you what the hour actually paid. A mileage figure on its own never told anyone whether the round was worth doing.
DropLane doesn't keep the GPS running all day. It sits quietly until it notices you've left where you parked, records while you're moving, and goes back to sleep when you stop.

faq.q: Do I have to press start?
faq.a: No — and there's no button to press. That's the whole point. If you have to remember, you'll forget on the day it matters.

faq.q: What if I forget to sort a drive?
faq.a: Nothing is lost. Unsorted drives wait on the Days screen, and the app nudges you rather than guessing for you.

faq.q: Will my route history end up somewhere?
faq.a: No. There's no account and no server. Everything lives on your iPhone, and backs up only to your own iCloud if you want it to.

faq.q: I drive a bike, not a van.
faq.a: That works. Cargo-bike miles are recorded the same way. The built-in mileage rates are for motor vehicles, though, so what a bike can claim depends on your country and your circumstances — worth asking an accountant.

faq.q: Is my country's mileage rate in there?
faq.a: Seventeen countries have their official rate built in and kept current. Anywhere else, type your own rate once and the app does the maths.

faq.q: Can I use it in kilometres?
faq.a: Yes. Miles or kilometres, your own currency, and the fuel price you actually pay — all in Settings, on the first screen.

faq.q: Does it work where there's no signal?
faq.a: Yes. Recording runs off your iPhone's own GPS and wants no internet at all. Drives taken out of signal come back labelled “Start” and “End” instead of street names, and DropLane fills those in the next time it sees Wi-Fi. A week down lanes with no bars still adds up right.

faq.q: What happens when I get a new phone?
faq.a: Sign in to the same iCloud and your drives, earnings and expenses come back on their own. There is no account to make and no password to lose, because there was never a server holding any of it — the backup is yours, in your own iCloud.

faq.q: What if I stop paying — do I lose my records?
faq.a: Nothing is deleted. Your drives stay on the iPhone and in your own iCloud, exactly where they were. But DropLane needs an active subscription to open, so if you want the figures somewhere else, export the CSV before you go. It's in Settings, and it's one tap.

faq.q: How do I know what fuel really cost before the card invoice arrives?
faq.a: Tell DropLane the price per litre your fuel card charges, then log the litres when you fill up. The cost is worked out on the day, so the week's profit is right weeks before the invoice turns up.

closer_body: Fourteen days free, no account, and nothing to remember at six in the morning.
